original: If a path is not shown it does not mean that it is not public, it may have rights but they are not yet recorded or formalised.
simplified: Paths that are shown on the map are public paths.  Paths that are not shown might still be public paths.  A path that has rights of access will not be shown if the rights have not yet been recorded or legalised.

original: Customary tenants, the most significant of which were copyholders, held land by an agreement made at the manor court which was entered on its roll, a 'copy' of which was regarded as proof of title.
simplified: People who rented houses, especially people called 'copyholders', made an agreement with the owner of the house at the manor court. They wrote the agreement in the court's record book. The person who rented the house got a copy of the agreement which they could show to prove that they were allowed to live in the house.

original: Part of the current HAPs is to identify which of these target sites need to be maintained, which need restoration, and which are suitable for the creation of habitat.
simplified: There are three important tasks carried out under the HAPs.  First, identifying which of these target sites needs to be looked after; second, working out which need restoration; and finally, deciding which might be suitable for creating places for wildlife.
